question: creatures that spit out a token whenever they attack
trap: The trigger is worded as 'whenever ~ attacks', 'whenever you attack', and 'whenever ~ and/or another creature attacks', and Krenko makes tokens off a tap ability rather than an attack trigger.
notes: Adeline reads 'Whenever you attack' rather than 'Whenever Adeline attacks' - vetter should decide whether that counts. I think it should.

question: Whenever a creature dies, each opponent loses life and I gain it. What are all the Blood Artist effects?
trap: Some versions drain every player, some only opponents, some only your own creatures, and some phrase it as 'target player loses 1 life' - text search for one phrasing badly under-matches. Vindictive Vampire is a near-miss only if you require lifegain (it deals damage instead of draining and does not gain you life on all printings - vetter should confirm).
notes: [vetted by owner 2026-08-07] Vindictive Vampire moved expect_absent -> expect_present. expect_absent here is genuinely borderline; consider dropping it rather than risking a wrong golden.

question: permanents that ping each opponent whenever another creature enters under my control
trap: The trigger condition (creature ETB) and the effect (damage to opponents) are two separate clauses that plain text search cannot bind together; Goblin Bombardment deals the same damage but off a sacrifice cost, not an ETB trigger.

question: what gets me value every time a land hits the battlefield?
trap: Half these cards say 'Landfall' as a keyword and half spell out 'Whenever a land enters the battlefield under your control'; Azusa is the classic false friend since it enables land drops but has no trigger at all.

question: cards that do something every time I cast an instant or sorcery
trap: Magecraft keyword vs spelled-out 'Whenever you cast an instant or sorcery spell' vs 'Whenever you cast a noncreature spell' - three phrasings for one structural pattern. Guttersnipe is arguably a true positive (it triggers on instants/sorceries) so it may need to move to expect_present.
notes: [vetted by owner 2026-08-07] Guttersnipe moved expect_absent -> expect_present. Guttersnipe is a bad absent - vetter should probably move it to present or delete it. Flagging honestly.

question: Cards that punish opponents for drawing cards
trap: 'Punish' is a paraphrase - the cards say 'deals 1 damage to that player' or 'loses 1 life'. Notion Thief looks related but is a draw-replacement effect with no trigger, so it fails a structural trigger->effect match.

question: o:'sacrifice an artifact' as an activation cost, not an effect
trap: The exact same words appear as a cost (before the colon) and as an instruction in an effect ('sacrifice an artifact: ...' vs 'you may sacrifice an artifact'), and text search cannot see the colon boundary.
notes: Deliberately phrased in Scryfall-ese to vary register. Good probe of whether the system models cost-vs-effect position.

question: creatures with an ability I pay for by discarding a card
trap: Merfolk Looter is the canonical trap: 'T: Draw a card, then discard a card' has the discard as an effect, not a cost, so a naive o:discard search over-matches badly.
notes: Zombie Infestation fits the pattern but is an enchantment, so excluded from expect_present given the 'creatures' constraint.

question: abilities where you pay life as part of the cost
trap: 'Pay N life' as a cost reads nearly identically to 'you lose N life' in an effect; Bitterblossom loses life as part of a triggered effect, which is a different structure entirely.
notes: Fetchlands are a large, boring chunk of the true answer set - vetter may want to scope this to nonland cards.

question: anything where the cost is exiling cards out of your own graveyard
trap: This pattern hides behind at least three surfaces - an explicit activation cost, the Delve keyword, and Escape - so no single oracle string finds them; Bojuka Bog exiles a graveyard as an effect and matches on words alone.
notes: [vetted by owner 2026-08-07] scoping resolved: keyworded alternative costs (delve, escape) are in scope. Whether keyworded alternative costs (delve, escape) count is a scoping call for the vetter. Worth keeping ambiguous to see how the system handles it.
scoping: Delve and Escape DO count as exiling cards from your graveyard as a cost. Bojuka Bog stays absent: it exiles a graveyard as an effect, not a cost.

question: cards where you tap OTHER untapped creatures you control to pay for something
trap: Crew N, Convoke, and spelled-out 'Tap an untapped creature you control' are the same structural cost wearing three different names; Cryptolith Rite grants a tap ability rather than using tapping as a cost.
notes: Heart of Kiran also has a counter-removal alternative; still a crew card.

question: stax pieces that tax my opponents' spells without taxing mine
trap: The asymmetry is the whole question - Thalia and Sphere of Resistance use nearly identical wording but tax everyone including you, so word-level matching cannot separate symmetric from one-sided taxes.
notes: Good probe of whether the system models the affected-player argument of a static effect.

question: permanents that change the rules about how many spells people can cast per turn
trap: These are rule-modifying continuous effects with no trigger and no activation; they read like nothing else in the game, and 'can't cast more than one spell' has several paraphrases.

question: stuff that lets me play cards off the top of my library
trap: A permission-granting static effect, not a draw or a tutor; Sensei's Divining Top manipulates the top of your library but grants no casting permission, and impulse-draw effects exile first so they are a different structure.

question: anything that lets me cast my spells at instant speed
trap: 'As though they had flash' is the key phrase but the question never says flash; Quicken grants the same effect to one spell as a one-shot rather than as a continuous permission.

question: cards that stop permanents from untapping during untap steps
trap: These modify the untap step itself (a rule-replacement/continuous effect) rather than tapping anything; Icy Manipulator taps permanents and matches on the shared vocabulary.

question: permanents that replace things going to the graveyard with exile
trap: Grafdigger's Cage is a prohibition, not a replacement, and Bojuka Bog is a one-shot exile - the structural distinction between 'instead' and 'can't' and 'do it once' is invisible to keyword matching.

question: Is there anything that soaks up damage aimed at me and takes it instead?
trap: Redirection ('is dealt to X instead') and prevention ('prevent that damage') are structurally different but use overlapping vocabulary, and the natural phrasing 'soaks up' matches neither.

question: fog effects - prevent all combat damage this turn
trap: Mostly easy for text search; the variance is in cards that prevent only damage dealt to you, or only by attacking creatures, which should arguably be excluded.
notes: Removed a low-confidence expect_absent. Included mainly as an easy calibration row; the real variance is cards that prevent only damage dealt to you or only from attackers.

question: cards that change what happens when I draw a card
trap: 'If you would draw a card, instead...' is a replacement on an event most cards only reference as an effect; Howling Mine adds draws without replacing any, and multi-draw effects flood a naive search.
notes: IMPORTANT: I believe the correct card name is 'Underrealm Lich', not 'Underworld Lich'. Vetter must fix the spelling before this row is used. [vetting: corrected Underworld Lich -> Underrealm Lich, verified against card store]

question: anything that makes damage hit for double or triple
trap: Multipliers ('deals double that damage instead') and flat adders (Torbran's +2) are the same idea to a player but structurally distinct replacement effects, and symmetric vs one-sided matters too.

question: creatures that come into play as a copy of something already on the battlefield
trap: 'You may have ~ enter as a copy' is a copy-replacement applied as the permanent enters, distinct from an ETB trigger that creates a copy token; Clever Impersonator is actually a true positive, which is the trap in reverse.
notes: [vetted by owner 2026-08-07] Clever Impersonator moved expect_absent -> expect_present. Clever Impersonator very likely belongs in expect_present (it enters as a copy of any nonland permanent). Vetter should move or delete it.

question: permanents that pull a creature out of my graveyard onto the battlefield when something happens
trap: Requires binding a trigger to a graveyard-to-battlefield move; graveyard-to-hand cards like Raise Dead share almost all their vocabulary but land the card in the wrong zone.

question: blink effects - exile my own creature and bring it right back
trap: 'Blink' and 'flicker' appear on zero cards; the actual text is 'exile target creature, then return it to the battlefield', which shares its opening clause with real exile removal.
notes: Return timing varies (immediately, end of turn, next end step) - vetter should decide whether all count.

question: tutors that put the card on top of my library instead of in my hand
trap: The destination zone is the only thing separating these from every other tutor, and it sits in a subordinate clause after nearly identical search text.

question: permanents that let me cast spells straight out of my graveyard
trap: This is a static casting permission that must be distinguished from self-recursion keywords (flashback, escape, disturb) and from cards like Snapcaster that grant flashback to one specific card.

question: how do I replay lands from my graveyard
trap: Extra-land-drop cards use nearly the same words ('you may play an additional land') but grant no graveyard permission at all.

question: removal spells that get rid of a creature without ever saying destroy or exile
trap: This is a negative constraint over semantic function - the system has to know that bounce, tuck, sacrifice-edicts and -X/-X all achieve removal, then exclude the two most common words for it.
notes: Flagged suspect: 'gets rid of' is a functional category, not a structural one. I expect the system either can't express the negation or can't express the functional grouping. Informative either way. [2026-08-07] Pongify moved expect_present -> expect_absent: its Forge node is SP$ Destroy and its oracle text opens 'Destroy target creature', so it cannot satisfy 'without ever saying destroy'. Flagged in compiled_questions.json judgment_calls since the harness was built; the golden was simply wrong.

question: cards that double the +1/+1 counters I put on things
trap: Hardened Scales adds one rather than doubling - the same replacement shape with a different arithmetic operator, which text search cannot tell apart.
notes: If the system treats Hardened Scales as a match, that's a precision failure worth recording rather than a bug in the question.

question: token doublers
trap: Terse search-box phrasing with zero oracle vocabulary in it; the actual text is 'If one or more tokens would be created under your control, twice that many are created instead'. Second Harvest copies existing tokens once rather than replacing token creation.

question: cards that proliferate off a trigger rather than as a one-shot spell
trap: Every one of these contains the literal word 'proliferate', so the discriminating work is entirely in the trigger-vs-activated-vs-spell distinction; Contagion Clasp proliferates from an activated ability.

question: anything that physically moves counters from one permanent to another
trap: Moving a counter is neither adding nor removing, and cards express it as 'move a counter from', 'put those counters on', and 'remove a counter... put a counter on' - three shapes for one operation.
notes: expect_absent lists a mechanic name, not a card - vetter should replace it with an actual proliferate card or empty the list. [vetting: dropped 'Proliferate' from expect_absent - a mechanic, not a card]

question: abilities that trigger off a state-based action, like a creature hitting 0 toughness or a player hitting 0 life
trap: State-based actions are a rules concept that almost never appears in oracle text; 'dies' is the only common surface for one, so the question is asking for a category the card text doesn't name.
notes: Deliberately ill-posed. A good system should probably push back and ask what the player actually means rather than returning every death trigger.

question: creatures that when they die go find other creatures in my deck and put them straight onto the battlefield
trap: Three links have to hold at once - a death trigger, a library search, and a battlefield destination rather than hand or graveyard - and each link has its own paraphrases.
notes: Answer set is small; verify a couple more before finalizing.

question: cards that exile the top of my library and let me play those cards, but only for a limited time
trap: Exile-then-permission-then-time-limit is a three-part structure with no keyword; Bomat Courier exiles cards and later returns them to hand, matching most of the words and none of the structure.

question: what lets me untap my stuff on other people's turns so I can use tap abilities more than once a round?
trap: The stated goal (reuse tap abilities) is downstream of the actual text (untap permanents during another player's untap step or end step), so the search has to reason about why an effect is wanted, not just what it says.

question: free sac outlets that also replace the creature I sacrificed
trap: 'Free' (no mana in the cost), 'sac outlet' (sacrifice-a-creature as a cost you choose), and 'replaces' (draws or makes a body) are three constraints, one of which is player jargon that appears on no card.
notes: Left expect_present empty on purpose - I could not name one I was fully certain of that satisfies all three constraints. The absent cards are free sac outlets that do not replace the body.

question: cards that only trigger when an opponent chooses to do something voluntarily
trap: Voluntariness is not encoded in card text - 'whenever an opponent casts a spell' and 'whenever an opponent is dealt damage' look identical structurally, and the distinction lives in the rules, not the oracle.
notes: Deliberately included as a probe. If the system confidently answers this, that is a hallucination signal.

question: what goes infinite with an untapper like Kiki-Jiki?
trap: Comboing is an emergent property of two or more cards interacting, not a structural property of one card's text; the search would have to simulate loops across pairs.
notes: Deliberately out of scope. Worth keeping to see whether the system declines gracefully or fabricates. A player really would type this.

question: abilities I can activate as many times as I have mana for - nothing in the cost that limits it
trap: This is a constraint over what the cost does NOT contain (no tap symbol, no sacrifice, no counter removal, no once-each-turn rider) - a negative structural query rather than a positive pattern match.
notes: Flagged suspect because negation over cost components is the kind of thing a structural search may simply not express. The answer set would also be enormous, so it may be ill-posed on recall grounds too.
